title: Redwood cost-econ discovery with Tangent Capital
summary: Discovery focused on per-token economics and tradeoffs between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Customer running high-volume inference for doc summarization and assistant features; primary concerns: cost per token, latency SLOs, batching/caching levers, budget of ~$25k/mo initial, security needs (SAML, audit logs). Next steps: run cost model worksheet, propose Dedicated staging config, share security pack, schedule benchmarking POC.
next_steps: Redwood to send cost model spreadsheet and pricing sheet
Schedule 2-hour benchmarking POC with sample workloads (SE + customer)
Share security & SOC2 docs and VPC deployment checklist
Follow-up on Dedicated capacity options and commit pricing
action_items: Aisha Patel: Send cost model + pricing sheet (due: 2026-03-06)
Diego Ramos: Prepare benchmark plan and sample scripts for Summarization pipeline (due: 2026-03-10)
Lena Ortiz: Share sample tokenized workload and 7-day traffic spike patterns (due: 2026-03-09)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Aisha (AE), Diego (SE), Maya (SE) - Redwood; Lena (Head of ML), Mark (CTO), Priya (Infra), Kai (Procurement) - Tangent Capital

[00:00] Aisha: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is Aisha from Redwood, really appreciate you taking the time. we're joined by Diego and Maya on the engineering side. could we do quick intros?
[00:10] Lena: Sure hi I'm Lena head of ML at Tangent, we run the doc summarization product and the internal agent.
[00:15] Mark: Mark, CTO, short on time so i'll be here for the core cost questions.
[00:20] Priya: Priya, infra lead, looking at network and VPC constraints.
[00:24] Kai: Kai, procurement, i'll handle contract and budget questions.
[00:28] Diego: Diego, solutions engineer at Redwood, i'll walk through throughput and batching options.
[00:33] Aisha: Great thanks. Lena can you give 5-7 min overview of your workloads and what you're optimizing for?

[02:00] Lena: Yeah so primary workload is document summarization for our customer support product; average request length is 600 tokens input, output ~120 tokens, peak concurrency around 400 req/s during business hours but usually 80-120 req/s. We also have an internal chat assistant that's lower qps but needs <350ms p50 latency. goal is reduce inference cost and keep latencies acceptable, budget for initial roll is roughly $25k per month, could scale if value realized.

[03:15] Diego: ok good. couple quick clarifying q's, which models are you evaluating locally today?
[03:22] Lena: Mostly open models, we've experimented with Llama2-Chat variants and a custom fine-tuned Falcon 40b. Running on k8s with GPU nodes, but ops overhead is high.

[03:35] Maya: when you say fine-tuned Falcon 40b, are you running fp16 or int8 quantized?
[03:40] Lena: currently fp16; we haven't pushed quant to int8 nationwide.

[04:05] Aisha: Perfect context. today we wanted to walk through per-token economics and the levers you can pull - batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization, and capacity choices Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private - and make sure we align on a POC plan. sound good?
[04:18] Mark: yes. focus on what's cheaper long-term for your pattern.

[04:35] Diego: ok quick high-level - Hosted (our API) gives fastest time-to-value: pay per-token, no infra ops, cost looks like X per 1k prompt tokens + Y per 1k completion tokens on model tier; Dedicated is reserved GPU pools - lower per-token compute cost if you commit monthly and have high steady throughput; Private gives you our runtime in your VPC/on-prem for compliance but then you bear infra ops.

[05:20] Lena: rough numbers - can you give a concrete example, like our 600-in 120-out?

[05:30] Diego: sure; so for that payload you've got ~720 tokens per request. on Hosted with a medium LLM family we show roughly $0.80-$1.50 per 1k input tokens and $1.20-$2.50 per 1k output tokens depending on model latency and architecture, which translates to about $0.60-$1.80 per request at your averages, but remember that's without batching gains.

[06:10] Priya: those ranges are wide, what's driving the factor of 3x?

[06:14] Diego: two main drivers - model choice (40b vs 7b families), and batching/caching. with batching we can amortize kernel overhead across tokens and multiple requests, and with KV/prefix caching we avoid recomputing long prefixes for repeated contexts (e.g., same prompt templates). also quantization to int8 or q4 variants reduces compute and memory, which reduces cost on Dedicated.

[07:05] Lena: for our use most prompts have recurring system prompts and some repeated customer context, so caching might help. is KV cache effective across many different customers though?

[07:18] Maya: yes it's effective for prefix caching where customer-specific tokens are reused; our runtime supports per-customer namespace caches and TTLs. effectiveness depends on hit rate, we typically see 30-60% token savings in similar setups.

[07:55] Mark: ok say we get 40% caching hit and batching at 8 reqs average, what does that do to cost?

[08:05] Diego: ballpark with those levers you could see 2-3x improvement in per-token billable compute cost versus naive single-request runs. so that $0.60-$1.80 per request might drop to $0.20-$0.80. again model choice matters; smaller quantized models with same quality reduce further.

[09:10] Priya: latency tradeoffs - batching affects p50/p95, can you guarantee the <350ms p50 for our assistant?

[09:20] Diego: yes with continuous batching and dynamic batching thresholds we can meet p50 targets while still batching at low latencies. p95 is trickier; for p95 under 350ms we'd tune batch sizes and route some requests to low-latency pool (burst/dedicated nodes). Redwood routing can send latency-sensitive calls to dedicated low-latency nodes and cost-tolerant calls to higher throughput nodes.

[10:05] Aisha: also worth noting Dedicated offers predictable SLOs with reserved capacity and autoscale policies; Hosted is great but for consistent 400 rps peaks Dedicated usually lowers unit cost and gives tighter latency SLAs.

[10:30] Kai: procurement question - if we go Dedicated what's typical commit? monthly? annual? and how is overage handled?

[10:40] Aisha: common pattern is monthly reserved capacity with option to commit annually for discounts. overage we've got burst pools and pay-as-you-go top-up; we'll itemize in the pricing sheet.

[11:10] Lena: what about Private - we need SAML SSO and strict audit logs plus KMS integration, is that supported?

[11:18] Maya: yes Private supports SAML/SSO, RBAC, KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs. it's basically our control plane run in your VPC and optional on-prem runtime. security pack we'll share.

[12:00] Mark: ok, can you show a short worked example of cost math comparing Hosted vs Dedicated for our baseline month (assume 2M requests, 720 tokens average, 30% cache hit, batch size 6)?

[12:15] Diego: yeah quick calc - rough tokens processed: 2M * 720 = 1.44B tokens. with 30% cache hit you bill 1.008B tokens. if Hosted effective rate is $2 per 1M billable tokens (blended), that's ~$2,016 per month - wait that seems low, hmm let me re-check numbers aloud. (pause) actually i mis-specified the per-1M earlier; on medium model it might be $20-$40 per 1M depending on model family when including completion+context multipliers - so at $25 per 1M, 1.008B tokens -> 1008 * $25 = $25,200. so on Hosted you'd be near your $25k budget.

[13:40] Lena: ah that matches our expectations. how much could Dedicated save?

[13:45] Diego: Dedicated compute unit cost can be 2-3x cheaper for high steady throughput because you amortize GPU hours; with our example a 2x saving would put you ~ $12k-$13k plus infra premium and reserved commit. but there's setup, commit and minimums.

[14:10] Priya: ops overhead for Private is a factor too; we need team to run k8s and perf tune. any RU numbers to compare infra ops effort?

[14:20] Maya: Private requires internal ops but our Private offering includes the runtime and observability. typical teams see ~0.25-0.5 FTE for infra if they already have k8s expertise; otherwise more. Hosted removes that ops burden.

[15:05] Mark: about quantization - how confident are you on int8 for our fine-tuned Falcon 40b? any quality regressions?

[15:15] Diego: it depends on model and dataset; int8 and q4_0/q4_k configs often introduce small regressions. we recommend running evals on a holdout prompt set. Redwood Optimize will surface quality vs cost curves; in other customers we've seen <2-3% quality drop for big token reductions. we'll propose a small eval suite for you.

[16:00] Lena: ok please include eval. also curious about burst - if we commit Dedicated for steady traffic but see irregular spikes, do you auto-burst to Hosted?

[16:10] Aisha: yes routing policy can be configured to overflow to Hosted or to other regions/instance types. that's a common hybrid pattern: Dedicated for base, Hosted for overflow.

[16:35] Kai: procurement - if we do hybrid, can billing be consolidated? one invoice?

[16:40] Aisha: yes we can consolidate billing into single invoice and break out lines for Hosted and Dedicated usage.

[17:05] Lena: what about isolation and data residency? some of our customers require EU-only processing and logs not leaving region.

[17:12] Maya: we support region pinning and data residency with Dedicated and Private. Hosted has regionized endpoints as well; we'll need to validate specific retention policies for logs.

[17:45] Diego: quick note on caching - prefix/KV cache effectiveness increases with template use and repeated customer data; if your summarize calls reuse the same system prompt and a lot of the context is repeated, you could see sizeable savings. another lever is response caching for identical prompts at the app layer.

[18:30] Mark: are there any hidden costs: egress, storage of KV cache, logging retention?

[18:36] Maya: egress and storage are accounted for separately in Dedicated/Private; Hosted includes typical inbound/outbound but high volume egress may appear as an add-on. we'll annotate the pricing sheet with expected egress and storage tiers.

[19:05] Kai: timeline wise - we want a pilot in 3-4 weeks, does that fit your cycle?

[19:12] Aisha: yes we can do a 2-4 week benchmarking POC: Redwood provides staging Dedicated pool + Hosted sample traffic to compare. Diego will own the plan.

[19:40] Diego: i'll propose a concrete plan: we spin up a small Dedicated staging cluster equivalent to two A100-class nodes (or Ampere equivalent), run your 7-day traffic replay with and without caching & batching, and produce detailed per-token cost and latency breakdown.

[20:10] Lena: do you need sample data or just tokenized traces?

[20:15] Diego: tokenized traces are enough for performance; for quality evals we'll need the prompt/response pairs. we'll also want a 7-day spike pattern to simulate peaks.

[21:00] Priya: security docs?

[21:05] Maya: we'll send SOC2, VPC setup guide, KMS integration doc, and SAML SSO checklist.

[21:30] Mark: quick question about monitoring - can we get token-level costing and route-level latency breakdown in the console?

[21:38] Diego: yes Redwood Console gives per-route and per-model token cost breakdowns, p50/p95 latency trends, and trace links. We'll enable a dashboard for the POC.

[22:05] Kai: contract terms - minimum term on Dedicated?

[22:10] Aisha: we have month-to-month for staging and pilots; production Dedicated often uses 3-12 month commits with discounts. we'll include options.

[22:35] Lena: ok i'd like to prioritize these in order: 1) cost model + pricing sheet 2) benchmark POC 3) security docs 4) pilot contract options.

[22:50] Aisha: perfect we'll send that pack. any other questions?

[23:05] Mark: one last thing - can you do a worked sensitivity table showing cost at 20/30/40% cache hit and batch sizes 1/4/8?

[23:15] Diego: absolutely will include that in the spreadsheet; we'll show Hosted vs Dedicated blended costs and show break-even commit points.

[24:00] Lena: sounds good. quick note - we also benchmarked ModelServeX internally and saw good raw latency but the ops burden was high; curious how Redwood's managed tooling reduces that.

[24:15] Maya: our Console and Auto-batching along with automatic kernel selection reduce ops load; we'll demo the ops workflows in the follow-up SE session.

[25:00] Aisha: ok let's recap and confirm owners.

[25:10] Aisha: Redwood will send: cost model + pricing sheet (Aisha), benchmarking plan (Diego), security pack (Maya). Tangent will send: tokenized traces and prompt sets (Lena), procurement preferences (Kai).

[25:30] Kai: yes we'll aim to get procurement constraints within 3 days.

[25:40] Lena: we'll aim to share traces by next Monday.

[26:00] Aisha: great, we'll schedule the 2-hour benchmarking kickoff after we get traces. any blockers?

[26:10] Mark: nothing else from me.

[26:20] Priya: ensure the VPC checklist includes subnets and KMS IAM roles.

[26:30] Maya: will do.

[26:40] Aisha: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and share the calendar invite for the POC kickoff.

[26:50] (end of meeting)

Notes on quality: transcription has occasional word swaps and slight speaker mislabels; technical figures were discussed live and will be confirmed in the spreadsheet.
